summary.headline: 35 beamline sectors (the APS-U ring has 40 sectors; 35 carry ID/BM beamline ports, r50, r1); 71 beamline entries (54 ID, 17 BM) as listed on the APS Beamline Directory and the 2026-10-05 commissioning chart. APS-U delivered 9 new feature beamlines (POLAR 4-ID, XPCS 8-ID, CSSI 9-ID, ISN 19-ID, HEXM 20-ID, CHEX 28-ID, PtychoProbe 33-ID, 3DMN 34-ID-E, ATOMIC 34-ID-F), 15 enhancement beamlines (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 15, 25, 26, 27, 30, 32-ID) and a do-no-harm program covering 12 other ID beamlines and all BM beamlines; ASL at 25-ID is a relocated/new canted beamline built in APS-U scope and counted among the enhancements.

programFacts.fact: Nine feature beamlines; 15 enhancement beamlines; ~60 instruments and ~30 optical subsystems delivered or refurbished; do-no-harm covered 12 ID beamlines and all 18 BM beamlines; 70 ports qualified for operation.
All BM beamlines moved inboard by 42 mm with an additional 0.5 mrad inboard angular shift because the MBA lattice moved the BM source.

Completion (CD-4) review late Sept 2025; DOE final approval announced 2026-02-05; $815M project; 'nine new beamlines, along with enhancements of a further 15 and alignment of all 72 research stations'.
January 2026: upgrade work essentially completed with all scope delivered; nearly all beamlines back online.
During construction APS described the scope as seven feature beamlines plus infrastructure for two more (3DMN and Atomic at 34-ID).
FDR (2019): 19-ID (SBC-CAT) and 20-ID (spectroscopy, later moved to 25-ID) had to be vacated for the two long beamlines ISN and HEXM, whose end stations sit in the new Long Beamline Building.

Superconducting undulators: eight NbTi SCUs were planned for APS-U (FDR Table 3.24: 2x 16.5 mm/1.9 m in-line pairs, one 16.5 mm/1.5 m canted pair, one 18.5 mm/1.2 m canted pair); challenges in scaling magnet lengths and reducing periods caused magnet failures and fabrication delays; the IPAC'25 abstract (June 2025) expected two SCUs installed by late 2025 and six more to follow; as of 2026-09-22 no SCU is listed in any sector and sectors 1, 6, 11, 20 and 28 run on permanent-magnet devices.

BM sources after APS-U (FDR Sec. 3-4): the BM source point moved 42.3 mm inboard and 1.826 m upstream; as designed, a BM front end sees a combination of radiation from the M3 and M4 transverse-gradient dipoles plus the Q8 offset-quadrupole reverse bend (5.36 mrad), and the delivered fan is limited to ~5.4 mrad. The FDR anticipated that most BM beamlines (which use only ~1 mrad) would be realigned to view the 'clean' M3 source on the inboard side. Table 3.29 (6 GeV, 200 mA): M3 0.653 T, Ec 15.6 keV; M4 0.609 T, 14.6 keV; Q8 0.186 T, 4.5 keV; old APS BM 0.599 T, 19.5 keV at 7 GeV. MEDSI'25 confirms that all BM beamlines were moved 42 mm inboard with an extra 0.5 mrad inboard angular shift (which source each BM line now views is not stated beamline by beamline).

As-built front ends (MEDSI'25): 19 high-heat-load front ends (12 windowless, 7 with a 0.2 mm thick, 5.5 mm clear-aperture diamond window that replaced all beryllium windows) and 16 canted-undulator front ends; HHLFE heat-load limit 21 kW total and 590 kW/mrad^2 peak; a burn-through mask was added as first mask. The 7 windowed HHLFEs match FDR Table 3.1 (1-, 3-, 10-, 17-, 20-, 30-, 35-ID).

Pre-upgrade APS insertion devices were removed from the ring ahead of schedule in 2023 and retrofitted with new magnetic arrays and control systems before reinstallation (hence many as-built devices are 'short' canted versions, suffix S, in the Sept-2026 ID table).

enhancement.plain: 1-ID shoots very high-energy X-rays (about 40-140 thousand electron-volts) that can pass through centimetres of metal, to see stresses and crystal grains inside engine parts or batteries. The upgrade gave it a new, steadier sample-handling and detector system, and planned a new crystal 'colour filter' that bends the beam sideways so it does not smear out the much smaller, sharper beam of the new APS. A stronger superconducting magnet source is still to come.
enhancement.expert: FDR scope: (i) replace the vertically diffracting, cryo-cooled bent double-Laue Si(111) monochromator (fixed exit, 40-140 keV, ~1e-3 bandwidth) by the same Rowland-condition concept in the HORIZONTAL plane, because the phase-space compensation that preserved the old 40 pm.rad vertical emittance to within 20% would not hold for the APS-U ~4.2 pm.rad vertical emittance (FDR 1-ID section), and engineer it for the heat load of a long SCU; (ii) 1-ID-C sample-manipulation system with hexapod + tilt stage; (iii) 1-ID-E high-resolution SMS with continuous rotation + tilt (dark-field-capable diffractometer) and a +4 m end-station extension for pinhole SAXS to ~1 um features and a refractive-lens TXM below 200 nm at high energy (vs ~500 nm demonstrated at 45 keV in 6 m).

beamlines.summaryPlain: Maps where trace metals sit inside frozen cells and materials with a 50-200 nm X-ray spot.

enhancement.plain: 2-ID makes X-ray 'element maps' of cells, soils and microchips by scanning a tiny spot and recording the glow (fluorescence) each element gives off. The upgrade plan adds mirrors that keep the tiny new beam steady, a mirror-focused microprobe at 2-ID-E, and a new frozen-sample nanoprobe (Bionanoprobe-II) aiming for 10-nanometre detail. As of the latest sources, BNP-II was still being built (Sept 2025) and the 2026 beamline directory still describes 2-ID-E with zone-plate lenses, so the mirror microprobe is not yet confirmed.
enhancement.expert: FDR scope (FDR: whole 2-ID line to be canted in 2019, before APS-U; S02 now holds two short canted 2.8 cm devices): a vertically focusing mirror on each branch so that, with the existing horizontal bendable mirrors, the source is re-imaged stigmatically onto beam-defining apertures at ~35 m (stable secondary source, tolerant of the 2.5x vertical source-size change between timing and brightness modes; spec to 30 keV under full heat load); 2-ID-E: replace zone plates by figured in-vacuum KB mirrors (60-80% vs 10-20% efficiency; achromatic, allows pink-beam/multi-harmonic XRF) with BDA, compact interferometers and <10 nm, >10 mm-travel fast stages - predicted focus gains of ~1e2 (micro-XAS) and ~1e4 (micro-XRF); 2-ID-D: BNP-II cryogenic nanoprobe, <10 nm resolution, few-atom sensitivity, ptychography-enhanced XRF.

2-ID-E: enhanced microprobe (BDA, figured in-vacuum KB mirrors, interferometers, fast stages)

beamlines.operator: XSD Inelastic X-ray & Nuclear Resonant Scattering (IXN)
techniques: nuclear resonant scattering (NRIXS/NRVS, NFS, synchrotron Mossbauer)
beamlines.summaryPlain: Tunes X-rays to make atomic nuclei (57Fe, 83Kr, 151Eu, 161Dy) resonate, revealing atomic vibrations and magnetism, even at deep-Earth pressures.

enhancement.plain: 3-ID uses X-rays tuned extremely precisely (to about a thousandth of an electron-volt out of 14,400 - better than one part in ten million) so that they make the nuclei of special atoms like iron-57 resonate ('ring'), revealing how atoms vibrate inside rocks squeezed to the pressure at Earth's core or inside enzymes. The upgrade added mirrors that squeeze the beam to about a micrometre, so tiny samples in diamond pressure cells can be measured.
enhancement.expert: FDR scope: new KB system in 3-ID-C for 1 x 1 um focus (from ~20 um) at multiple resonant energies with an option to focus 43.2 keV for XRD, and ~5 um at the dual-fast-shutter position 4 m downstream (vs 13 um) for 57Fe SMS (48-bunch -> artificial 6-bunch); DAC work to ~300 GPa and 3000 K. Contingent on funding: new inline cryogenic, dispersion-compensated 57Fe HRM (0.6 meV FWHM, reduced tails, ~100x energy-alignment stability, switchable to eV bandpass at 14.4/43.2 keV for XRD). Not APS-U funded but enabled by the lower horizontal divergence: move the HERIX-3 IXS spectrometer to 3-ID-D (+80% Q range).
fdrDeliverables: (operating funds) relocation of IXS spectrometer to 3-ID-D
enhancement.asBuilt: 2026 directory: micro-focusing in 3-ID-B and 3-ID-C to ~1 x 1 um^2 or 1 x 12 um^2; HRMs for 57Fe (1 meV at 14.4 keV), 83Kr, 151Eu, 161Dy; cryo-cooled Si(111) HHLM 7-27 keV; 3-ID-D now 'nuclear resonant scattering with dual fast shutter system' and 'instrument development' (no IXS spectrometer listed). SEES (May 2025): 57Fe NRIXS/NFS available with a 1.5 x 12 um (H x V) focus; ~10 x 10 um planned for Kr/Eu/Dy. An energy-domain Mossbauer spectrometer was under development for late 2025. Undulators installed are 2.7 cm (not the FDR 2.5 cm).

The upgrade built a long vacuum 'telescope' tube so the detector can sit far away, added lenses to focus the beam onto it, and moved the ultra-small-angle (USAXS) instrument here and rebuilt it.

enhancement.plain: 27-ID does resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS): it measures the tiny energy X-rays lose when they kick electrons and magnetic waves in quantum materials. Some of its spectrometer motion stages were more than 30 years old, and the point where all its rotation axes should meet wandered by about 0.2 mm (two or three hair widths), so the upgrade rebuilt it to be far more precise and to fit bigger sample environments. It was the first APS-U enhancement to be finished, in March 2022. (APS News described the old instrument as 'two-decades-old'; the FDR says some motion stages were 'more than 30 years old'.)

(19-ID, the other long-beamline port, had been home to SBC-CAT, which no longer operates there - its pages now use the past tense; that program did not move to 25-ID.)
classification.expert: Relocation and canted-undulator expansion of the 20-ID spectroscopy program (plus the 11-ID-D laser pump-probe program and 7-ID time-resolved XAS) onto 25-ID, one of only two open ID ports at the time of the FDR. It has its own FDR section (4-10) and engineering documents (Table 4.2: ASL FRD APSU_2024251, photon delivery APSU_2012714) and appears among the 15 enhancement beamlines (Table 4.3, 25-ID: LN2 Si/multilayer monochromators and LERIX spectrometer). It is not counted among the nine feature beamlines (MEDSI'25; Feb 2026 completion news). The 2026-10-05 progress chart labels 25-ID-D,E 'ASL'.

asl.tagline: Two undulator beams side by side: one turns X-ray 'colours' into chemical maps, the other films chemistry with laser flashes and reads soft-X-ray edges with hard X-rays.
asl.plainSummary: Every chemical element gives off X-rays of its own 'colour' when it is hit by X-rays, and the exact shade shifts a little depending on whether the atom is rusted, charged or bonded to its neighbours. ASL at Sector 25 is built to read those tiny shifts. Two undulators sit side by side in the storage ring and send out two beams at a slight angle to each other. Mirrors push the beams further apart, so two independent beamlines can work at the same time. The outboard-going branch (25-ID-C) is a microprobe: it focuses X-rays to a spot about 1-2 micrometres wide (roughly a fiftieth of a human hair; a zoom lens can go from 0.5 to 10 micrometres) and maps which elements are where and what chemical state they are in, for example arsenic in a fern, metals in a battery electrode or a single monolayer of platinum. The inboard-going branch feeds two hutches. 25-ID-D does X-ray Raman scattering: hard X-rays bounce off light atoms like carbon, oxygen or lithium and lose exactly the energy that a soft X-ray would have needed. That lets scientists study those atoms inside thick cells, batteries or diamond pressure anvils, where soft X-rays could never reach. 25-ID-E is a 'stop-motion camera': a laser flash starts a chemical reaction and an X-ray pulse arriving a few hundred trillionths of a second to a thousandth of a second later records how atoms and electrons have moved.
asl.expertSummary: Canted 2.8 cm undulator pair (1 mrad) with first-optics horizontal mirrors that cross the beams: an inboard-reflecting bendable mirror on the outboard (upstream) source feeds the LERIX/time-resolved branch (25-ID-D,E), and two outboard-reflecting mirrors (flat + bendable, ~2.5 mrad each) on the inboard (downstream) source feed the advanced-spectroscopy microprobe (25-ID-C). Both branches have independent small-offset LN2-cooled Si(111)/double-multilayer monochromators in 25-ID-B (Si 4-40 keV; multilayers 5-20 keV, ~3% bandpass, d~24 and ~48 A stripes). 25-ID-C: KB microprobe (1-10 um zoom, Be-lens zoom 0.5-10 um), confocal XRF, micro-XAFS, HERFD (3 x 0.5 m analysers), miniXS/von Hamos XES (multi-element, simultaneous multi-edge), dispersive XANES with a bent polychromator, grazing-incidence XAFS. 25-ID-D: X-ray Raman scattering (LERIX heritage; LERIX-II prototype with half-metre analysers, asymmetric XRS with imaging). 25-ID-E: laser-pump/X-ray-probe TR-XAS, TR-XES, TR-XS from ~200-300 ps to 1 ms.

source.note: Values in r6 are calculated for 6.0 GeV, 200 mA at the device minimum gap; N includes end poles (effective N = N-2). 74 x 2.8 cm = 2.07 m, consistent with the FDR 2.1 m. Branch assignment (design): FDR Fig. 4.71 draws the UPSTREAM undulator beam going to the IRM (-> LERIX/TR branch, 25-ID-D,E) and the DOWNSTREAM undulator beam going to ORM1/ORM2 (-> AS microprobe, 25-ID-C); FDR text says the IRM sits on the outboard source and the ORMs on the inboard source, consistent with the upstream device giving the outboard beam (as for 34-ID in 3dmn.json). As-built confirmation not found.
source.plain: Two undulators, each about 2 metres long, sit one behind the other in the same straight section. Each is a pair of magnet arrays above and below the electron beam whose polarity flips every 1.4 cm (a 2.8 cm repeat), so the electrons wiggle and emit a bright X-ray beam. Small canting magnets steer the electrons by one thousandth of a radian between the two undulators, so the two X-ray beams leave about 1 mm further apart for every metre travelled.

frontEnd.fdr: Canted-undulator front end handling two beams 1 mrad apart, 10 kW each; windowless (differential pump) exit; 2 mm x 1 mm (H x V) exit aperture per branch (Sec. 4-10.4). FDR Table 3.1 lists 25-ID as canted, differential pump; the generic CUFE description gives two 2 x 2 mm apertures.

scienceCases.title: Dilute and difficult XAFS
scienceCases.plain: Measuring the chemistry of an element present at tiny concentrations, or inside a pressure cell, or in a film only one atom thick.
scienceCases.expert: Undulator brilliance for very dilute systems, small samples in high-pressure cells and glancing-angle thin films (e.g. Pt monolayer on SrTiO3).

scienceCases.title: Chemical imaging with X-ray emission
scienceCases.plain: Making maps that show not just where iron is, but whether it is rusted or not, pixel by pixel.
scienceCases.expert: FDR goal: emission spectra in ~1 s at microprobe spot sizes (vs 30-60 s before) -> simultaneous XES + XRF imaging; multilayer mono for a further 10-20x for non-resonant XES.

scienceCases.title: Light elements inside working devices (X-ray Raman)
scienceCases.plain: Seeing oxygen, carbon or lithium inside a sealed battery or diamond cell using hard X-rays, which soft X-rays cannot do.
scienceCases.expert: Non-resonant XRS gives soft-X-ray-like edges (O K, Li K, TM L/M) bulk-sensitive and free of self-absorption, with q-dependent access to non-dipole transitions.

scienceCases.title: Watching photochemistry
scienceCases.plain: Filming how a light-driven catalyst or quantum dot changes in the first billionths of a second after a laser flash.
scienceCases.expert: TR-XAS/TR-XES/TR-XS from ~100s of ps to ms fills the gap between XFEL femtosecond and quick-XAFS millisecond methods; e.g. Co-Pi OER catalysts under bias (Energy & Fuels 2025).

whatAPSUEnables.plain: A brighter, smaller source lets the microprobe squeeze the beam to about half a micrometre without losing working space.
whatAPSUEnables.expert: FDR: higher flux at beam sizes down to 0.5 um while retaining working distance and confocal detection (pre-upgrade 20-ID microprobe: 2-5 um).

whatAPSUEnables.plain: Spectra that took a minute now take about a second, so they can be recorded at every pixel of an image.
whatAPSUEnables.expert: FDR estimate: XES 30-60 s -> ~1 s at the same spot size with the MBA source; multilayer mono for another 10-20x.

whatAPSUEnables.plain: Switching to multilayer mirrors instead of crystals lets 10 to 100 times more X-rays through, when perfect colour purity is not needed.
whatAPSUEnables.expert: SPC: multilayer (3% bandwidth) gives 10-100x the flux of Si(111); directory: 1e15 vs 1e14 ph/s at 10 keV (25-ID-C).
